item.title: Prototyping 3D Game Locations for Levels with AI
item.description:
We've seen AI draw characters, buildings, and assets (even with sprites). But what about designing locations and levels? For our test, we'll take ten locations created for an imaginary 3D fantasy RPG with a significant touch of low-poly aesthetics. Our designers will be Nano Banana Pro, Grok Image 2, the flagship Qwen Image 3, and the budget Seedream 5.0 Lite. Read more

item.title: Demand Forecasting: Nothing More, Nothing Less
item.description:
Sales forecasting is like weather forecasting – it can only be done with a certain degree of approximation. Tens of thousands of items, thousands of locations, promotions, logistics, and other influencing factors – you can account for the maximum number of details, and there will still be random events that don't fit into any formula. However, even if perfection is unattainable, you can build a forecast that deviates from it only slightly. My name is Yulia Trusova, and I am the Head of the Logistics domain at Lenta Tech. In this article, I will explain how demand forecasting works and how modern methods help minimize this error. For those who want to delve deeper into the topic and technical details, our article "How Machine Learning Helps Lenta Group Forecast Demand" may be of interest. Read more

item.description:

item.title: Pentesting AI Components: What Vulnerabilities to Look For and What to Do About Them for CISOs
item.description:
The article is by Igor Sokolov, an ABP2B specialist. It focuses on AI component vulnerabilities, practical attack scenarios, and security issues when integrating artificial intelligence into corporate systems. Recently, AI in web applications was mostly limited to chatbots. Today, AI is entrusted with much more: access to internal documents, corporate email, CRM, databases, and sometimes even the ability to perform actions independently. For employees, these changes might seem minor: a smart search in the corporate portal, an assistant in CRM, or automated support ticket processing. While familiar tools become more convenient, the information security landscape changes significantly. Standard web pentesting still covers authorization, access control, APIs, user input, and business logic. However, a language model now sits between the user and the application, not just processing information but interpreting its content. If the model has access to external tools, text processing can lead to real actions within the corporate system. This opens new avenues for attackers. Instead of bypassing application restrictions directly, they can influence the AI component to retrieve data or perform operations autonomously. Read more

item.title: The Mathematical Theory of Why We Are Doomed to Self-Destruction and Can We Avoid It?
item.description:
One of the most frightening properties of technological civilization is that we don't even need malicious intent for a man-made catastrophe, let alone some secret shadow conspiracy—basic mathematics of non-cooperative games is enough. In systems theory, this is described by a situation where the locally correct calculation of each individual player deterministically guarantees collective self-destruction. In this article, we will discuss why this happens, how Computer Science and mechanism theory help to crack the prisoner's dilemma, and whether cooperation can be made the only mathematically correct scenario. Read more

item.title: tbook Four Months Later: Readers, Dictionaries, and v2 of the Format
item.description:
In July, I wrote about searching for a foreign language e-reader and the birth of the TBook format. Half of that article was about getting cheap LLMs to produce alignment without positional drift. Four months have passed since then. An app has been released on Google Play, a desktop reader for three OSs has appeared, along with offline dictionaries, an online converter with a shared library and a Telegram bot, a GUI converter with ready-made binaries, two dozen reports on translation quality experiments—and most importantly, the second version of the format. Read more

item.title: [Translation] Getting the Most out of BERT: Tokenization 50x Faster
item.description:
Even checking ordinary characters can become a bottleneck in text processing for language models. Profiling bert-base-uncased revealed that normalization took 88% of the tokenization time. In this article, we'll explore how SIMD instructions, Unicode caching, and skipping unnecessary operations helped speed up processing by about 50 times, why results differ across languages, and where this approach has limitations. Let's break down the optimization.

item.title: How I Wrote a Linter for the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Found Bugs in Anthropic's Official Servers
item.description:
If you're writing MCP servers for Claude Desktop or Cursor, you know how easy it is to catch a non-obvious bug: • A stray console.log() in stdout breaks the JSON-RPC protocol and completely freezes the client. • If a dangerous tool (like database/file deletion) lacks the destructiveHint annotation, the agent will execute it without user confirmation. • Prompt Injection can be embedded into tool descriptions, tricking the model into leaking context. I wrote mcp-linter (without any third-party dependencies, pure Node.js/TS): — 34 protocol and security check rules — Server health score from A+ to F (0-100) — Auto-fix generator (--fix) — Export to SARIF v2.1.0 for GitHub Security and a ready-to-use GitHub Action Try it in one line: npx mcp-linter -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory Repository: https://github.com/bakhtiyor-aminzoda/mcp-doctor Secure yourself

item.title: Life After Blocking: Neural Networks Have Changed My Profession, and I Don't Want to Work the Old Way Anymore
item.description:
Recent incidents with Anthropic blocking have made me seriously consider how I'll work if my account gets banned. In an instant, I realized how much my engineering profession has changed. It's only been about a year, but I already recall the previous way of doing things as something very distant from my past life. But the most important thing is this: I realized that I'm afraid of going back... and here's why.
